title: kube-proxy warns when mode is not set explicitly

detection.reason: the condition is the ABSENCE of the mode field, and the projection carries the mode only when it is present — an absent key cannot be told apart from a ConfigMap the agent has not re-synced

quote: In `v1.37`, `kube-proxy` will warn if the field is not explicitly set as part of the planned transition to nftables as the default mode in a future release.
remediation: Set `mode` explicitly in the kube-proxy config rather than relying on the default. The default is planned to become `nftables` in a later release, so a cluster that never named its mode gets a data-plane change it did not ask for on some future upgrade.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | startswith("kube-proxy")) | (.data // {}) | to_entries[] | .value | scan("(?m)^ *mode: *\"?([a-z]+)") | .[0]'  # empty output means the mode field is not set explicitly, which is what 1.37 warns about

title: ipvs mode deprecated since 1.35

detection.reason: read from the kube-proxy ConfigMap's own mode field; a mode passed only as a --proxy-mode container arg is not read here

quote: Added a (delayed) warning that `kube-proxy`'s ipvs mode is deprecated since `v1.35` and users on newer Linux kernels should be using the nftables mode instead, which became GA in `v1.33`.
remediation: Move to `nftables` on nodes with a recent kernel, or `iptables` on older ones. kubeadm now warns about this on every upgrade until the mode changes.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | startswith("kube-proxy")) | (.data // {}) | to_entries[] | .value | scan("(?m)^ *mode: *\"?([a-z]+)") | .[0]'  # prints the configured kube-proxy mode; ipvs is deprecated since 1.35
